      "source": [
        "# Simulating biophysically detailed multi-compartmental models using ISF"
      ]
    },
    {
      "attachments": {},
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "This notebook guides the user on how to use ISF to run *in silico* current injection experiments using biophysically detailed full-compartmental models using the [Simulator](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/simulator/index.rst) and [Evaluator](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/evaluator/index.rst) objects. These objects can be configured once per cell, and re-used for various simulation protocols.\n",
        "\n",
        "[Tutorial 1.2](./1.2%20Evaluation.ipynb) will show how to evaluate existing biophysically detailed compartmental models\n",
        "\n",
        "[Tutorial 1.3](./1.3%20Generation.ipynb) will use the concepts outlined in this Tutorial and [Tutorial 1.2](./1.2%20Evaluation.ipynb) to generate biophysically detailed compartmental models that satisfy the empirical constraints outlined in [Tutorial 1.2](./1.2%20Evaluation.ipynb).\n",
        "\n",
        "Adapt your desired output path below. Here, the results of the tutorials will be saved."
      ]
    },
    {

      "source": [
        "## Equipping a morphology with biophysical parameters"

      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "Which format do these parameters need to have?"
      ]

            "            'Myelin': {'properties': {'Ra': 100.0, 'cm': 0.02},\n",

      ],
      "source": [
        "from getting_started import example_data_dir\n",
        "import ast\n",
        "import pprint\n",
        "\n",
        "cell_param_file = I.os.path.join(\n",
        "    example_data_dir,\n",
        "    'biophysical_constraints',\n",
        "    '86_C2_center.param')\n",
        "\n",
        "\n",
        "with open(cell_param_file, 'r') as f:\n",
        "    params = f.read()\n",
        "pprint.pp(ast.literal_eval(params))"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "The variable `cell_param` is one big dictionary-like object, including information on:\n",
        "\n",
        "- the spatial distribution of ion channels\n",
        "- $Ca^{2+}$ buffering dynamics\n",
        "- default simulation parameters (time interval and resolution)\n",
        "- recording site locations\n",
        "- passive properties (capacitance, input resistance, and reversal potentials)\n",
        "- a morphology file"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "Using these parameters, we can create a [Cell](../../api_reference/single_cell_parser/cell/index.rst) object, containing all the information on morphology and simulation data in a Python wrapper. For our usecase, we need to pass an additional argument to scale the apical dendrite of the L5PT with. Why this is necessary is outlined [here](../auxiliary%20notebooks/A.1%20Morphology%20Reconstruction.ipynb)"
      ]

      "source": [
        "from single_cell_parser.cell_modify_functions.scale_apical_morph_86 import scale_apical_morph_86\n",
        "import neuron\n",
        "h = neuron.h\n",
        "I.logger.setLevel(\"INFO\")  # verbose output to see what is happening\n",

        "We now have a biophysically detailed [Cell](../../api_reference/single_cell_parser/cell/index.rst) object. Let's start by figuring out some general morphological properties of the example cell"

    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 5,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "stdout",
          "output_type": "stream",

            "total length = 16340 micron\n",

          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "length = sum([\n",
        "    sec.L for sec in cell.sections])\n",
        "dendrite_length = sum([\n",
        "    sec.L for sec in cell.sections if sec.label in ['Soma', 'Dendrite', 'ApicalDendrite']])\n",
        "soma_area = sum([\n",
        "    sec.area for sec in cell.sections if sec.label == 'Soma'])\n",
        "apic_area = sum([\n",
        "    sec.area for sec in cell.sections if sec.label == 'ApicalDendrite'])\n",
        "\n",
        "print('total length = {:.0f} micron'.format(length))\n",
        "print('total dendritic length = {:.0f} micron'.format(dendrite_length))\n",
        "print('soma area = {:.0f} micron^2'.format(soma_area))\n",
        "print('apical dendrite area = {:.0f} micron^2'.format(apic_area))"

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "## The ISF [Simulator](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/simulator/index.rst)\n",
        "\n",
        "This [Cell](../../api_reference/single_cell_parser/cell/index.rst) object can be simulated using NEURON's Python API, as outlined in [this auxiliary tutorial](../auxiliary%20notebooks/A.2%20Neuron%20API.ipynb). However, ISF provides convenient wrappers for simulating fixed stimuli.\n",
        "\n",
        "This Section will provide a walkthrough on how to interact with the biophysical properties of a [Cell](../../api_reference/single_cell_parser/cell/index.rst) using the [Simulator](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/simulator/index.rst) object, rather than directly interacting with the NEURON hoc interface. This object can be configured once per cell, and re-used for various simulation protocols. It operates on biophysical parameters of the `pandas.dataFrame` type.\n",
        "\n",
        "We will load in an existing configuration to showcase the syntax. More information on how this [Simulator](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/simulator/index.rst) object can be configures is given in [Tutorial 1.3: Generation](./1.3%20Generation.ipynb)."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "### Biophysical parameters"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 8,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "# Load example biophysical models\n",
        "from getting_started import example_data_dir\n",
        "model_db = I.DataBase(I.os.path.join(example_data_dir, \"simulation_data\", \"biophysics\"))\n",

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "Apart from the passive properties, we have 35 biophysical parameters, relating to varying biophysical aspects for the soma, axon (AIS), apical dendrite, and other dendrites (taken to be passive for current injection experiments).\n",
        "\n",
        "|Name|Meaning|Unit|\n",

        "|ephys.X.\\<location\\>.gXbar| Density of Hodgkin Huxley-type channel X |[$S/cm^2$]|\n",

        "|ephys.CaDynamics_E2_v2.\\<location\\>.gamma| Ratio of free $Ca^{2+}$ | None|\n",
        "|ephys.CaDynamics_E2_v2.\\<location\\>.gamma | Time constant of first-order dynamic $Ca^{2+}$-buffering| [$ms$]|\n",

      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "### The [Simulator](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/simulator/index.rst)\n",
        "\n",
        "Here, we introduce the [Simulator](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/simulator/index.rst) object, specific to a particular morphology."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "To set up a Simulator, you need morphology-specific fixed parameters. We will use a new morphology for this, with the ID \"89\"."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 11,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "def get_example_fixed_params(db, key):\n",
        "    p = db[key]['get_fixed_params'](db[key])\n",
        "    return p"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 12,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "stdout",
          "output_type": "stream",
          "text": [
            "{'BAC.hay_measure.recSite': 294.8203371921156,\n",
            " 'BAC.stim.dist': 294.8203371921156,\n",
            " 'bAP.hay_measure.recSite1': 294.8203371921156,\n",
            " 'bAP.hay_measure.recSite2': 474.8203371921156,\n",
            " 'hot_zone.min_': 384.8203371921156,\n",
            " 'hot_zone.max_': 584.8203371921156,\n",
            " 'hot_zone.outsidescale_sections': [23,\n",
            "                                    24,\n",
            "                                    25,\n",
            "                                    26,\n",
            "                                    27,\n",
            "                                    28,\n",
            "                                    29,\n",
            "                                    31,\n",
            "                                    32,\n",
            "                                    33,\n",
            "                                    34,\n",
            "                                    35,\n",
            "                                    37,\n",

            "                                    54,\n",

            "                                    60],\n",
            " 'morphology.filename': '/gpfs/soma_fs/scratch/meulemeester/project_src/in_silico_framework/getting_started/example_data/simulation_data/biophysics/89/db/morphology/89_L5_CDK20050712_nr6L5B_dend_PC_neuron_transform_registered_C2.hoc'}\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "fixed_params = get_example_fixed_params(model_db, '89')\n",
        "pprint.pp(fixed_params)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "These parameters define recording locations for stimuli, and some celltype-specific variables. In our case of an L5PT, it also defines the \"hotzone\": a small section of apical dendrite near the bifurcation zone that has a high density of $Ca^{2+}$ channels. Each L5PT morphology also has a free parameter to scale the diameter of the apical dendrite. This is added to the `fixed_params` as an additional modification method. Usually, big parts of such setup can be re-used for different morphologies, simulations etc. The setup below will highlight which parts are specific to the celltype, the cell, or the biophysical details of a single cell.\n",
        "\n",
        "The full setup of a Simulator object for running Hay's protocols on an L5PT is given in [biophysics_fitting.hay.default_setup.get_Simulator()](../../api_reference/biophysics_fitting/hay/default_setup/index.rst)."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 13,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "from biophysics_fitting.hay.default_setup import get_Simulator\n",
        "from biophysics_fitting.L5tt_parameter_setup import get_L5tt_template_v2\n",
        "\n",
        "def scale_apical(cell_param, params):\n",
        "    assert(len(params) == 1)\n",
        "    cell_param.cell_modify_functions.scale_apical.scale = params['scale']\n",
        "    return cell_param\n",
        "\n",
        "s = get_Simulator(fixed_params)\n",
        "s.setup.cell_param_generator = get_L5tt_template_v2\n",
        "s.setup.cell_param_modify_funs.append(('scale_apical', scale_apical))"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "We now have a Simulator object with morphology-specific `fixed_params`.\n",
        "\n",
        "For a Simulator object `s`, the main functions are:\n",
        "\n",
        "|Method|Output|\n",
        "|---|---|\n",
        "|`s.run(params)`| a dictionary with the specified voltagetraces for all stimuli|\n",
        "|`s.get_simulated_cell(params, stim)`| params and cell object for stimulus stim|\n",
        "|`s.setup.get(params)`|a cell with set up biophysics|\n",
        "|`s.setup.get_cell_params(params)`| cell `NTParameterSet` structure used for the single_cell_parser.create_cell. This is helpful for inspecting, what parameters have effectively been used for the simulation|\n",
        "|`s.setup.get_cell_params_with_default_sim_prams(params, ...)`| complete neuron parameter filethat can be used for further simulations, i.e. with the `simrun` module|"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "#### The $bAP$ stimulus\n",
        "\n",
        "The $bAP$ stimulus protocol is a step current injection at the soma, strong enough to evoke a backpropagating action potential (bAP)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 14,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "cell, param = s.get_simulated_cell(p, 'bAP')"
      ]
    },

        "Where exactly do we inject the epsp-shaped apical current? We already saved this information in `fixed_params`. Morphology \"89\" has a rather deep bifurcation, so the epsp injection is at only $295\\mu m$ from the soma."

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "#### Running all stimulus protocols\n",
        "\n",
        "In the previous sections, we ran an example $bAP$ stimulus, and a $BAC$ stimulus. This resulted in a single AP, and a triplet respectively. In order to verify if the biophysical properties of the cell match empirically observed responses, we also need to run $3$ step currents and measure the response.\n",
        "\n",
        "For this, we have a Simulator that has these step currents set up:"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 19,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "s = get_Simulator(fixed_params, step=True)\n",
        "s.setup.cell_param_generator = get_L5tt_template_v2\n",
        "s.setup.cell_param_modify_funs.append(('scale_apical', scale_apical))"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 20,
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "# may take a while, especially the step currents\n",
        "voltage_traces = s.run(params=p)"
      ]
    },

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
